standard_prerequisites.use: Finite-presentation approximation and descent of flatness, Tor exactness, polynomial-ring global dimension, local flat/free criterion and finite free resolutions. The local fibrewise-exactness and final cokernel arguments are retained as author proof, not removed.

core_obligations: Descend the data and pointwise flatness to a finite-type Noetherian stage, then pass to a polynomial presentation with bounded fibre projective dimension.
Construct and spread a finite free syzygy resolution over one neighbourhood, retain the complete fibrewise-exactness argument, and infer flatness of the original cokernel.

difficulty_reason: The arbitrary-base statement needs both finite-stage descent and a specifically chosen finite syzygy resolution whose exactness spreads on every fibre. That two-stage construction remains a concrete H2 argument after foundational homological algebra.

editorial_notes: Public1510 assumes locally finitely many weakly associated base points and a finite-type sheaf; it uses the usual finitely-presented openness theorem as input. This task proves the latter for arbitrary base rings. Neither hypothesis set is merely the same renamed assertion.

The source describes the localized polynomial fibre global dimension as n; the needed bound is at most n, which suffices for the nth syzygy. One may add dummy polynomial variables to avoid the harmless n=0 indexing convention.
